How to use it

  1. Enter the Chinese characters if you have them. Pinyin input only gives the Mandarin-based systems.
  2. Check the readings table. Some characters have several pronunciations (乐 Yue/Le, 曾 Zeng/Ceng); ★ marks the automatic choice.
  3. Pick a preset matching the person’s background — Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore/Malaysia, etc.
  4. Start with Core, copy the query, and widen to Extended or Exhaustive if you get few hits.
  5. Never rely on the name alone — confirm hits with date of birth, ID numbers, companies or addresses.

Check a spelling tests whether a spelling from a screening hit fits the name, or guesses its system. Batch handles a list of names at once. Wade-Giles input (Chiang Ching-kuo) suggests pinyin readings.

Tips: put each variant in quotes; use proximity search in professional databases (Li w/2 Keqiang); ignore honorifics such as Tan Sri, Datuk or Dato’ in Malaysian sources.

Limits

  • Western, adopted or personal names (Jack Ma, Carrie Lam, Sudono Salim) cannot be predicted.
  • Southeast Asian spellings were often recorded by ear; dialect given names are best guesses, surnames are hand-curated.
  • Hong Kong married names (陈方安生) need Surname length = 2.
  • Only pinyin and Wade-Giles can be typed in; for dialect spellings enter the characters.
